pageHelp.activity: This page shows what indexarr has done: feed updates, searches received from apps, grabs and logs. Use the tabs to find a failed run or a slow search, and read the cause and the suggested action. It exists so problems can be diagnosed without reading the server logs.
pageHelp.app: This page connects indexarr to Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr and the other apps, and lists the download clients. Use Connect an app to let indexarr create and update the indexers inside the app; use the manual address only for apps that accept a Torznab URL. It exists so you do not copy addresses and keys by hand.
pageHelp.app_form: This page connects one app to indexarr. Enter the address you use in the browser and the app API key; indexarr creates the indexers inside it and keeps them updated. Use it once per app, and open the connection again only when its address or key changes.
pageHelp.client_form: This page adds a download client, the program that receives the torrent or NZB. Choose the software, enter its address and password or key, and say which protocol it handles. Use it when downloads should start automatically instead of being saved by hand.
pageHelp.definition: This page shows one site definition: its state, version, categories and settings. Use Create indexer to start from it, or the advanced tools to inspect it. It exists for diagnosing a site that does not behave as expected.
pageHelp.definition_form: This page creates or replaces a definition from its YAML. Paste the definition, validate it, and save it only if you trust its source. Use it when a site is not in the catalogue yet.
pageHelp.definitions: This page lists the site definitions that indexarr can use. Use it to check the state and version of a definition, or to create an indexer from one. It is a tool for advanced users: normal use starts from Add indexer.
pageHelp.discover: This page shows the feeds found on a site address. Choose the feed you want and add it as an indexer. Use it when a site has no native definition but publishes an RSS or Atom feed.
pageHelp.home: This page tells you at a glance whether indexarr is working and what to do next. Read the status box first, then the suggested next step; use the address and key here when an app asks for them. It exists so you do not have to read logs or documentation to know where you stand.
pageHelp.import: This page imports indexers from Prowlarr or Jackett without changing them. Choose the manager, review the preview, then apply the plan. Use it when you already have a working manager and do not want to add every site again.
pageHelp.indexer_add: This page helps you choose a site without reading a catalogue of two hundred names. Start from what you need, read the one-line reason and what the site requires, try five real results, then add it; Show all sites opens the full catalogue. Use the guided path the first time and the full list when you already know the site you want.
pageHelp.indexer_detail: This page is the working page of one site: its health, the latest releases, the filters and its settings. Use Test and the refresh action to check it, and Edit to change its credentials or categories. It exists so every problem and every setting of a site stays in one place.
pageHelp.indexer_form: This page adds or edits one site. Fill only the fields the site requires, leave the rest in Advanced, and press Add and test to save and check it immediately. Use it when a site needs an account, a cookie or a special address.
pageHelp.indexers: This page lists the sites indexarr can search, one row per site, with their health. Use the search box or the row menu to test, update or disable a site; press Add indexer to add a new one. It exists so you can see in one place what is working and what needs attention.
pageHelp.maintenance: This page shows the database size, backups and cleanup tools. Use Backup now before an upgrade and restore only when you need to go back. It exists so your data can be protected and kept under control.
pageHelp.release: This page shows one release with its sources, size, seeders and download link. Check the details and press Download to send it to the client. Use it to understand where a result came from or why a download failed.
pageHelp.rules: This page lists the rules that hide or block releases. Add a rule with a simple pattern and remove it when it is no longer needed. Use it to keep unwanted results out of search and out of the apps.
pageHelp.run: This page shows one update run: what it fetched, what it kept and what it discarded. Read the reason of a discarded item when a site returns fewer releases than expected. It exists to explain what happened in a single run.
pageHelp.search: This page searches all your indexers at once and shows the releases they return. Type a title, narrow the results with the filters if needed, and press Download to send a release to your download client. Use it to check that a site really has what you need before adding it to Sonarr or Radarr.
pageHelp.settings: This page holds the settings of indexarr, divided into sections. Change one section at a time and press Save at the bottom of that section; secrets stay hidden until you ask to see them. Use it when you need to change the public address, the API key, the network or the maintenance schedule.
pageHelp.setup: This page is the first-run guide: address, import, sites and apps, in four steps. Follow the steps in order or skip the guide and reopen it later from Settings. It exists so the first working search takes a few minutes.
pageHelp.title: What this page is for, how to use it, and why

settings.additionalKeysHelp: Use one key per client (Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, a script). The primary key above cannot be revoked here; use the regenerate button.
settings.apiKeyHelp: Clients send this key as the request parameter
settings.apiKeyRotateHelp: Rotating it breaks every configured client until they are updated.
settings.apiRateLimit: API requests per key per minute
settings.apiRateLimitHelp: 0 = unlimited. Applied to the primary and every additional key; excess requests receive HTTP 429.
settings.autoDisableHelp: 0 = never. A successful run resets the counter.
settings.backupDirActions: List, download and restore from Maintenance.
settings.backupIntervalHelp: Checked every 30 seconds; the first backup runs soon after enabling.
settings.backupKeepHelp: Older automatic backups are removed. Pre-restore copies are kept.
settings.backupsEnabledHelp: A consistent copy of the database, made with SQLite
settings.breakerCooldownHelp: Pause after repeated failures or an HTTP 429/503 without Retry-After.
settings.breakerThresholdHelp: Consecutive failures before a host is paused.
settings.clearRunsConfirm: Delete run history older than the chosen number of days?
settings.clearTorrentsConfirm: Delete stored .torrent files? Magnets and metadata are kept.
settings.dangerText: Deleting every release empties the cache. The next run rebuilds it from the indexers.
settings.dbRowsValue: releases %d · indexers %d · history %d · rules %d · saved searches %d · API keys %d
settings.seedersTTLHelp: How old a source swarm must be before it is queried again.
settings.dedupeConfirm: Merge rows that share an infohash?
settings.downloadClientHelp: Adds a “Send to…” button on every release detail.
settings.error.downloadClient: Download client must be none, qbittorrent or transmission
settings.error.downloadClientURL: Download client URL must be an absolute http:// or https:// address
settings.error.flaresolverrInvalid: FlareSolverr URL must be an absolute http:// or https:// address
settings.error.flaresolverrURL: FlareSolverr URL must be an absolute http:// or https:// address, or empty
settings.error.passwordMismatch: The two passwords do not match
settings.error.passwordRequired: Set a password for the web interface, or leave the user empty to disable authentication
settings.error.passwordShort: The password must be at least 8 characters
settings.error.publicURL: Public URL must be an absolute http:// or https:// address, or empty
settings.error.telegramPair: Set both the Telegram token and chat ID, or neither
settings.error.userRequired: Set a user name together with the password
settings.error.webhookURL: Webhook URL must be an absolute http:// or https:// address, or empty
settings.fetchTimeoutHelp: Per request towards indexers and feeds.
settings.fetchTorrentsHelp: When off, only magnets and metadata are stored.
settings.flaresolverrHTTP: FlareSolverr solved the page but returned HTTP %d
settings.flaresolverrHelp: When an RSS feed or a direct indexer answers with a Cloudflare challenge, indexarr retries the same request through FlareSolverr. Leave empty to disable. Jackett and Prowlarr usually handle Cloudflare themselves, and a LAN address is never routed through FlareSolverr. The indexer URL, including its API key, is sent to FlareSolverr.
settings.flaresolverrOK: FlareSolverr OK: solved %d bytes; the URL has been saved
settings.flaresolverrTestHelpAfter: through the URL above; a successful test saves the URL and can take up to a minute.
settings.flaresolverrTimeoutHelp: How long FlareSolverr may spend on one Cloudflare check. The default is 60 seconds.
settings.historyRetentionHelp: How long run metrics, app searches and the last sample are kept. 0 keeps them forever; the default is 30 days.
settings.hostBurstHelp: Tokens available immediately before the rate applies.
settings.keyRegenerated: New API key generated: update every Torznab client
settings.liveSearch: Search indexers live on a cache miss
settings.liveSearchCacheHelp: How long a live fan-out result stays cached. 0 disables the cache.
settings.liveSearchHelp: When the cache has no result, ask enabled Torznab indexers and store what they return. Off by default: it can make a client wait.
settings.liveSearchTimeoutHelp: Overall deadline for the live search. Indexers that do not answer in time are ignored.
settings.liveSearchWaitHelp: The aggregate waits up to 5 seconds, but returns as soon as every indexer has finished. Indexers still running after the cap appear in Activity and are cached for the next request.
settings.maxTorrentSizeHelp: Larger downloads are rejected instead of stored.
settings.maxTorrentsHelp: Only items that expose a .torrent link but no magnet need a download.
settings.newPasswordHelp: At least 8 characters. Leave empty to keep the current one.
settings.noKeys: No additional keys. Add one for each client that should have its own revocable key.
settings.openWarning: The web interface is open to anyone who can reach the port. Set a user and password, or keep it behind a trusted network/reverse proxy.
settings.pruneConfirm: Delete releases outside the retention window?
settings.publicURLHelp: The address your apps use to reach indexarr. It appears in the endpoint shown on Home and App.
settings.purgeDaysConfirm: Delete releases not seen in the chosen number of days?
settings.purgeIndexerConfirm: Delete every cached release from the selected indexer?
settings.purgeNoLinksConfirm: Delete releases with neither a magnet nor a .torrent?
settings.regenerateConfirm: Generate a new API key? Every Torznab client will stop working until updated.
settings.removeConfirm: Remove the stored value? This cannot be undone.
settings.resetAPIUsageConfirm: Reset request counters for every API key?
settings.resetErrorsConfirm: Clear the last error and open circuit of every indexer?
settings.restoreConfirm: Restore this backup? indexarr restarts and replaces the current database.
settings.restoreHelp: Upload a validated backup. It is staged and applied when indexarr restarts; the current database is copied aside first.
settings.retentionHelp: 0 keeps everything. The cleanup runs every six hours and can be triggered from Maintenance.
settings.revokeConfirm: Revoke this API key? Its client will stop working.
settings.secretEmptyHelp: Leave empty to keep the current value.
maintenance.help.integrity: Runs the full PRAGMA integrity_check and reports the verdict.
maintenance.help.quick: Runs PRAGMA quick_check: faster than the full check.
maintenance.help.foreign: Runs PRAGMA foreign_key_check and reports orphaned rows.
maintenance.help.vacuum: Rebuilds the file and returns free pages to disk.
maintenance.help.optimize: Runs PRAGMA optimize and checkpoints the WAL.
maintenance.help.checkpoint: Writes pending WAL frames and truncates the WAL file.
maintenance.help.analyze: Runs ANALYZE to rebuild query-planner statistics.
maintenance.help.reindex: Runs REINDEX; useful after a large deletion.
maintenance.help.resetErrors: Resets error state and backoff without re-enabling the indexer.
maintenance.help.dedupe: Keeps the oldest row per infohash and the best data.
maintenance.help.clearTorrents: Shrinks the database; clients receive magnets instead of files.
maintenance.help.prune: Uses the retention configured in Settings.
maintenance.help.purgeDays: Deletes releases older than the chosen number of days.
maintenance.help.purgeIndexer: Removes only releases supplied by the selected indexer.
maintenance.help.purgeNoLinks: Rows without magnet or .torrent cannot be used by clients.
maintenance.help.clearRuns: Removes only run history; releases and indexers stay.
maintenance.help.resetAPI: Clears per-key request counters; keys keep working.
maintenance.help.deleteAllHelp: Empties the cache; the next source run rebuilds it.
maintenance.dangerText: Deleting every release empties the cache. The next source run rebuilds it.
maintenance.optimized: Planner statistics refreshed and WAL checkpointed
maintenance.checkpoint: WAL checkpoint: %d frame(s) written and WAL truncated
maintenance.checkpointPending: WAL checkpoint incomplete: %d of %d frame(s) still pending
maintenance.needRetention: Set retention days in Settings first
maintenance.torrentsCleared: %d stored .torrent file(s) removed; magnets were kept
maintenance.purgedDays: %d release(s) not seen in the last %d day(s) removed
maintenance.apiReset: API usage counters reset for %d key(s)
maintenance.deleteConfirmWord: Type DELETE in the confirmation field

settings.setupHelp: Reopen the four-step wizard to change the address, import sites or connect an app.
settings.storedLimitHelp: Soft limit: activating another search-only site shows a measured warning first. 0 disables the warning. Currently stored: %d.
settings.storedLimitNote: The warning always shows measured numbers: releases per day, estimated MB per month and the current database size. Raising this limit does not change those numbers.
settings.storedRetentionHelp: Only releases that came exclusively from a stored source and are older than this are removed. Favorites and downloads are never touched. 0 keeps them forever.
settings.subtitle: Choose a section. Each one saves on its own.
settings.telegramChatHelp: Set both Telegram fields, or neither.
settings.telegramTokenHelp: Optional; it needs the chat ID too. The token is encrypted in the vault.
settings.torznabEndpointLabel: Endpoint to give to Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr…
settings.vaultHelp: Back up this key separately: without it the stored secrets cannot be opened.
settings.vaultInData: The key is in the data directory: move it outside before copying the data folder.
settings.vaultUnavailable: The vault is not available: native indexer secrets and app keys cannot be saved.
settings.webhookHelp: Receives a JSON POST for the selected events. The URL is encrypted in the vault. Leave it empty to keep it unchanged.
setup.address.help: Leave empty to use the address this browser is using.
setup.address.label: Public address
setup.address.text: Use the address other machines on your network can reach.
setup.address.title: How your apps reach indexarr
setup.address.verifyHelp: Keep the address stable: changing it later means updating every app.
setup.app.text: indexarr adds the new indexers to the app by itself.
setup.app.title: Connect Sonarr or Radarr
setup.import.readOnly: No external manager: sources are configured and searched by indexarr directly.
setup.import.text: Pick sources from indexarr's native catalog. Jackett and Prowlarr are not needed: indexarr replaces them.
setup.import.title: Add your sources
setup.sites.empty: No ready-made site available: use the full list.
setup.sites.text: These public sites need nothing else. Add them now and test them later.
setup.sites.title: Choose the sites
setup.skipped: Setup skipped. You can reopen it from Settings → General.
setup.subtitle: Four short steps to the first search.

storeWarning.note: The site is read every 30–60 minutes with jitter; duplicates are merged. The estimate is measured now and can vary with the site.
storeWarning.probeError: The trial read failed, so the estimate is unavailable: %s
storeWarning.probeErrorNote: You can cancel and try again later, or confirm knowing that the numbers are missing.
storeWarning.subtitle: You are about to memorise the new releases of %s. There are already %d stored sources; the soft limit is %d.
storeWarning.title: This is another stored source
storeWarning.window: Measured from %d items read from the site latest list.
tip.activityTabs: Updates are feed runs, Searches are requests from apps, Grabs are downloads sent to clients.
tip.addAdd: Adds the site to indexarr. You can remove it later without losing stored releases.
tip.addConfigure: This site needs settings such as a URL or an API key: fill them in before adding it.
tip.addGuided: Start from what you need: indexarr recommends a few sites and explains why.
tip.addNeed: Choose what you are looking for; the recommendations change accordingly.
tip.addNeedsInfo: What you must provide before the site works: nothing, an account or a cookie.
tip.addProvidesInfo: What the site returns: magnet or .torrent links, seeders, search results or only new releases.
tip.addReliability: Verified: tested by the catalogue. Testing: not proven yet. Unofficial mirror: a copy of the original site.
tip.addShowAll: The full catalogue with filters. Use it when the recommended sites are not enough.
tip.addTry: Shows up to five real results from this site before you add it.
tip.appApiKey: Found in the app under Settings → General → API Key.
tip.appClient: Download clients receive the torrent or NZB. They are not apps that indexarr configures.
tip.appClientDefault: The default client receives releases when the protocol matches.
tip.appClientProtocol: Torrent clients receive magnets and .torrent files; Usenet clients receive NZB files.
tip.appDelete: Removes the connection in indexarr. Indexers already in the app are left alone.
tip.appLastSync: When indexarr last contacted the app. A sync is not a download.
tip.appManual: Use this only for apps that accept a Torznab address, like gextto. indexarr does not configure those apps for you.
tip.appName: Only a label inside indexarr; the app keeps its own name.
tip.appStatus: Green: the last sync worked. Red: the last sync failed; open the row for the reason.
tip.appSyncLevel: How much indexarr may change in the app. Full sync also updates existing indexers.
tip.appSyncNow: Sends the current indexer list to this app now.
tip.appType: Sonarr for series, Radarr for films, Lidarr for music, Readarr for books.
tip.appURL: The address you use in the browser, including the port. Do not add /api.
tip.clientCategory: The category or label the client shows for indexarr downloads.
tip.clientDefault: Used when no other client matches the protocol.
tip.clientEnabled: Disabled clients stay configured but receive nothing.
tip.clientKind: The software running at that address.
tip.clientPaused: Adds new downloads paused, so you can choose what to start.
tip.clientProtocol: Torrent for qBittorrent, Transmission and Deluge; Usenet for SABnzbd and NZBGet.
tip.indexerAccess: Public sites need no account; private sites need the credentials in their settings.
tip.indexerDelete: Removes this indexer from indexarr. Releases already stored are kept.
tip.indexerEnabled: Disabled indexers stay configured but are not searched or synced.
tip.indexerInterval: How often indexarr reads the new releases. 0 uses the default from Settings.
tip.indexerPriority: Lower numbers are tried first when two indexers return the same release.
tip.indexerRun: Reads the new releases now instead of waiting for the schedule.
tip.indexerSearchOnly: This site has no new-release list: it only answers searches.
tip.indexerState: Verified means the catalogue has tested it; Testing means it may still fail.
tip.indexerSync: Pushes this indexer to the connected apps on their next sync.
tip.indexerTags: Tags let Sonarr and Radarr choose this indexer for specific categories.
tip.indexerTest: Runs a real search and a download test now.
tip.languageSelector: Changes the interface language. It does not change the sites you use.
tip.navProblems: Number of indexers or apps that need attention now.
tip.releaseAge: Time since the site published or indexarr first saw the release.
tip.releaseFavorite: Favorites are never removed by retention.
tip.releaseHidden: Hidden releases stay in the database but do not appear in search.
tip.releaseLeechers: How many peers are downloading. Not a quality measure.
tip.releaseSeeders: How many peers have the complete file. Higher is usually faster.
tip.releaseSize: — means the site did not provide the size, not zero.
tip.settingsSecret: The value stays hidden until you press Show. Empty means unchanged.
tip.statusDot: Green: working. Amber: partial data. Red: problem. Grey: disabled.
tip.storeLatest: This site has a real new-release list: you can ask indexarr to keep it in the database.
application.footer: indexarr creates its indexers in the app with the “indexarr · ” prefix and only ever changes those. Use a tag filter when one app must see a subset of your sites, for example 4K only in the 4K Radarr.
application.restoreSummary: Restore of %s: %d added, %d updated, %d deleted, %d skipped
application.snapshotUnsupported: %s does not allow indexer snapshots: indexarr cannot manage its indexers.
application.tagFilterHelp: Only the indexarr indexers with at least one of these labels are sent to this app. Separate labels with commas; leave it empty to send every indexer.
application.tagFilterWhere: Edit the labels on the indexer card, in the “Tags” field.
applications.footer: indexarr writes only the indexers whose name starts with “indexarr · ”. It adds missing ones, updates changed ones and removes the ones that are no longer selected, then leaves everything else in the app as it is. The tag filter narrows which indexarr indexers belong to an app; an empty filter sends all of them. A restore is a recovery tool: the next sync applies the current indexarr state again.
applications.restoreConfirm: Restore the indexarr indexers of %s to this snapshot? Indexers you created by hand are not touched. A new snapshot of the current state is saved first.
applications.snapshotsEmpty: No snapshot yet: one is saved automatically before the first change, or use “Snapshot now”.
applications.snapshotsHelp: Before every sync that changes something, indexarr saves the app's indexer list. Restore brings the indexers indexarr created back to that state; indexers you created by hand are never touched.
tip.appRestore: Brings the indexarr indexers back to this snapshot. Hand-made indexers are left alone.
tip.appSnapshot: Save the app's current indexer list now, without changing anything.
tip.appSnapshotIndexers: How many indexers the app had when the snapshot was taken.
tip.appSnapshotList: Snapshots are kept newest first; the last 20 per app are stored.
tip.appSnapshotReason: Before sync: taken automatically before a change. Manual: saved by you. Before restore: taken automatically before a restore.
tip.appTagFilter: Only the indexarr indexers with one of these labels are synced to this app. Empty means every indexer.
tip.appTagFilterAll: No tag filter: every enabled indexarr indexer is sent to this app.
tip.idxTags: Labels used by each app's tag filter. Comma-separated, for example tv, anime, 4k.
settings.notificationsIntro: Choose the channels, which events to send and how long to wait before repeating the same event. indexarr sends a short message in the interface language, with a link to the relevant page when the public address is set.
settings.channelsHelp: At least one channel must be configured. The webhook receives a JSON POST; Telegram needs both the bot token and the chat ID.
settings.webhookStoredHelp: The URL is stored encrypted in the vault. Leave the field empty to keep it unchanged; use Show to read it.
settings.telegramStoredHelp: The token is stored encrypted in the vault and never appears in the page. Leave it empty to keep it unchanged.
settings.eventsHelp: Each switch enables or disables one kind of notification. A state notification is sent only when the state changes, not on every error.
settings.notifyNewReleasesHelp: One message per pass, with the count and the first titles.
settings.notifyFailuresHelp: An indexer that becomes unreachable, blocked or degraded, and when it is healthy again. One notification per state change.
settings.notifyGrabFailedHelp: After every copy of the same release failed: title, application and a readable reason.
settings.notifyCatalogUpdatedHelp: New or changed definitions when the catalog is reloaded or updated.
settings.notifyBackupFailedHelp: Only when the automatic backup job is enabled.
settings.notifyCooldownHelp: The same event (kind and source) is not sent more than once in this interval. New releases are grouped per pass and skip this wait.
settings.testHelp: Send a test message now to the configured channels, without waiting for the anti-spam window.
settings.notificationsHelp: Notifications never block searches or runs: they are sent in the background with a timeout. Channel secrets are encrypted in the vault and never appear in the logs. When no channel is configured, indexarr sends nothing.
notify.test: indexarr test notification: the channel works.
idx.catalog.coverage: Coverage: %d ready sources, %d with known software, %d to write.
tip.catalogToWrite: This source has no native route yet: it stays queued until one is written and verified.
indexer.error.managerEndpoint: indexarr replaces Jackett and Prowlarr: use the tracker URL or a catalog source. Manager endpoints are not accepted.
